items.definition: Small boat carrying 20-30 passengers or cargo such as wine or sand across the river; sometimes used for fishing; flat-bottomed and keelless.
Square sail, one of the sail types a boat could carry; also used on the Barco Rabelo.
A sprit-type sail that the Barquinho do Rio Minho could carry as an alternative to the square sail.
Flat bottom hull form with no keel, used by river boats such as the Rabelo.
Keel; the Rabelo and the Barquinho do Rio Minho lack one, having flat bottoms.
Very simple boat from Vila Praia de Âncora, shaped like a wooden bread-kneading trough, used for sea, coastal and river fishing.
Yard of a bastard lateen sail, set on a small mast forward on the Maceira.
Typical flat-bottomed Douro boat carrying wine casks down river to the Gaia cellars, with a square sail.
Wine casks, the cargo the Rabelo carried along the Douro to the Gaia cellars.
Raised structure rising roughly amidships and aft on the Rabelo, near where the steering oar is worked.
Long steering oar of the Rabelo, worked from a raised platform, used instead of a rudder.
Raised platform aft on the Rabelo from which the steering oar is handled.
Boat from Valbom able to sail river and sea, used for fishing, cargo and ferrying passengers; has a small shelter.
Small shelter on the Valboeiro protecting and comforting passengers.
Name given to a Valboeiro according to its cargo use (bakers' goods); the other name is barco das toucinheiras.
Name given to a Valboeiro or Avintes boat according to its cargo use (bacon).
A long-bladed steering oar used in place of a rudder on Rabelo, Valboeiro and Avintes boats.
items.term: remo de pá longo em vez de leme

items.definition: Douro boat classified by cargo, with an awning and passenger benches, and a pendant sail on a forward mast.
Pennant-type sail set on a mast forward on the Barco de Avintes.
Protective awning fitted over the Avintes boat for passengers.
A family of boats from Póvoa: large lancha for hake, smaller types for sardine, longline and whiting fishing; mast can be lowered.
Smallest Lancha Poveira type, used to fish whiting (faneca), about 4-5 metres long.
Trapezoid-shaped sail carried by the Lancha Poveira on a mast that rakes aft and can be unstepped.
Mast that could be taken down; on the Lancha Poveira it leans aft.
Boat of the Ria de Aveiro for gathering and carrying seaweed (moliço), also cargo and livestock; low sides, shallow draft, brightly painted bow and stern.
Draft; the Moliceiro's minimal draft lets it travel the many shallow canals.
Towing from the bank, used as a means of propulsion besides sail on the Moliceiro.
Pole used to push the boat along, a propulsion method of the Moliceiro besides sail.
Rudder; the Moliceiro is steered by a large rudder worked by a tiller crossing amidships.
Entirely black, undecorated boat from Ílhavo, similar to the Moliceiro, normally crewed by three.
Triangular sail type rigged on many of these traditional fishing boats, often several per vessel, giving speed and handling under sail.

numbers.what: latin sails on the Rasca de Pesca

items.definition: Name of one of the lateen sails on the Rasca de Pesca's complex four-sail rig.
Main sail, listed among the four lateen sails of the Rasca de Pesca (text is truncated).
Describes a boat that sails very well; the Rasca's complex rig made it extremely fast and responsive under sail but needed a large crew.
High freeboard, meaning the hull sides stand high above the waterline, as on the Rasca de Pesca.
Continuous flush deck running the length of the boat, found on the Rasca de Pesca and Muleta de Arrasto.
The rig: the arrangement of masts and sails; a complex rig demanded a numerous crew.
Forward rake of the masts; both masts of the Barco da Pescada leaned markedly forward and had different heights.
Oars used to propel or manoeuvre the boat, arranged a set number per side.

numbers.what: oars per side on the Bateira

items.definition: Mast raked slightly aft, as on the Bateira, carrying a long triangular lateen sail.
The bow, the front of the boat; its shape (curved, rounded) characterises each boat type.
Covered stern section of the hull, a feature of the Bateira.
Bow thwart (bench) to which the mast is fixed on the Bateira and Barca da Ericeira.
Crew; its size varies by boat type and its work, such as fishing or rowing.
Type of purse-seine style fishing for which the Nazaré Galeão was used.
Hatches on the deck giving access to the fish holds below.
Fish holds below deck where the catch is stored.
Transom stern, a flat-panel stern shape, as on the Lancha da Sardinha and Canoa Caçadeira.
Tiller-type rudder, mounted on the transom stern of the Lancha da Sardinha.
Hybrid (bastard) lateen sail, a variant of the lateen rig used on the Lancha, Barca, Caíque and Canoa.
Trawling, dragging a net while fishing; the Traineira manoeuvred with oars to keep the boat across (broadside).
Outboard rudder mounted on the outside of the hull, as on the Traineira and Barca da Ericeira.

numbers.what: Barca da Ericeira oars per side

items.definition: Two masts angled away from each other, as on the Caíque de Traquete.
Two masts of unequal size or placement, markedly raked forward, carrying bastard lateen sails on the Canoa Caçadeira.
Trawling with the boat broadside to its direction of drag, a particular feature of the Muleta de Arrasto.
Elegant decked sardine-fishing boat of Cascais and Sesimbra, fast and seaworthy, on which the sardines were salted aboard; sometimes raced.
A large lateen-type sail variant, rigged on the foremast of the canoa da picada and used on several Tagus boats.
A small aft sail (mizzen) carried in addition to the main lateen sail.
A rudder mounted inboard, as on the canoa da picada.
Sesimbra deep-sea fishing boat with a decked hull and two spritsails; masts were lowered and oars used during fishing.
Sprit-type sails, normally two, rigged by the Barca da Pesca do Alto.
Setúbal deep-sea fishing boat with a schooner-style rig, bowsprit, wide beam, decked hull and a lot of keel.
Bowsprit; a spar projecting forward from the bow, to which a small staysail is attached.
The most emblematic Tagus vessel: a heavy, bulging cargo boat with a gaff mainsail, two cabins and a towed boat.
Gaff sail, hoisted close to the mast and strongly raked aft, used as the fragata's mainsail.
Stay or staysail, a sail set on a forward stay; used on many Tagus boats.
A small boat towed astern, used to tow the fragata by rowing when needed.
Typical Tagus cargo boat, bulging yet more elegant than the fragata, keelless, with one or two staysails and a square-shaped sail.
False bulwarks that allowed better stowage of cargo.
Hold fitted with removable floor sections for storing cargo, as in the varino.
Early-20th-century decked Tagus boat with notched bow and sloping stern, used for fishing and carrying people and cargo across the river.
Side steering blades or paddles that helped with manoeuvring the batel.
Varino-family boat carrying people and goods across the Tagus, with a large lateen sail and a small staysail.
Fast, one- or two-masted Tagus boat carrying cargo and passengers, rigged with bastard lateen sails.
Fragata-like boat with a rounder bow, carrying heavy loads such as sand and stone; crew poled it in shallow water.
Long poles used by the crew to push the boat along in shallow water.
Decorated varino-family boat carrying pine branches, with a long triangular lateen sail on a short mast set far forward.
Smaller Tagus boat with a fragata-like hull whose stem curves smoothly into the keel; usually a large bastard lateen.
The stem; on the bote cacilheiro it blends continuously into the keel.
Smaller fragata-like boat used mainly to carry cargo and transship goods to and from anchored ships.
Transshipment: transferring goods between ships, the main job of the canoa cacilheira.
A staysail set on a stay; here tacked down to a pole serving as a bowsprit.
Tacked: the forward lower corner of a sail is fixed down, here to a spar at the bow.
Side steering oars or boards that greatly helped manoeuvring and navigation in the Tagus channels and creeks.
Narrow tidal creeks of the Tagus estuary through which these boats had to navigate.
A large blade rudder, removable, valuable as an aid for steering in the Tagus creeks and channels.
A toothed, strongly rounded bow shape characteristic of the Muleta do Seixal and echoed in the Riba-Tejo hull.
A mast strongly raked forward, from which the yard is hoisted; typical of the Muleta rig.
A yard: the spar from which a sail is hoisted and held.
To tack (fix the sail's forward lower corner) and to trim or sheet in a sail, done using spars extending from stern and bow.
Triangular lateen sails; the Caíque carries two large ones, and several other boats carry one or two.
A tiller-steered rudder mounted outside the hull, as on the Canoa do Espinel.
Lowering the sails, done by the Baleeira do Pico crew when chasing a whale so they can row.
A projecting pin or fitting at the bow that, with a pulley, helps haul in the catch.
A strong pulley (block) at the bow that eases hauling in the fish catch.
Open-mouthed (undecked or open-waisted) hull type, as in the Canoa do Espinel and carapau boat.
items.location: part 4 (Canoa do Espinel; Barco da Pesca do Carapau)
